mcq.q: How do you perform binary subtraction using 2’s complement?

options.A: Add the 1’s complement of the subtrahend to the minuend and add 1 to the result
options.B: Add the minuend and the subtrahend directly
options.C: Add the 2’s complement of the subtrahend to the minuend
options.D: Subtract the bits one by one starting from the least significant bit

mcq.answer_text: Add the 2’s complement of the subtrahend to the minuend

mcq.q: When performing binary subtraction using 1’s complement, what must you do if there is an end-around carry after addition?

options.A: Add the carry back to the least significant bit of the result
options.B: Ignore the carry and take the result as is
options.C: Subtract the carry from the result

mcq.answer_text: Add the carry back to the least significant bit of the result

mcq.q: Given two 4-bit binary numbers, 1101 (-3 in 2’s complement) and 0110 (+6), what is the result of their addition using 2’s complement arithmetic?
What is the main difference between 1’s complement and 2’s complement representation of negative numbers?

options.A: 1’s complement inverts all bits, while 2’s complement inverts all bits and adds 1
options.B: 1’s complement adds 1 to the binary number, 2’s complement does not
options.C: 2’s complement inverts all bits, 1’s complement does not
options.D: Both represent negative numbers the same way

mcq.answer_text: 1’s complement inverts all bits, while 2’s complement inverts all bits and adds 1

sq.q: Explain the Binary Coded Decimal (BCD) system in detail. How does it differ from pure binary representation? Provide the BCD representation for the decimal number 1947. Discuss the advantages and disadvantages of using BCD over pure binary.
answer: BCD System: BCD stands for Binary Coded Decimal. In this system, each decimal digit (0 to 9) is represented separately by its 4-bit binary equivalent. Instead of representing the entire number as a single binary number, each decimal digit is encoded individually.

BCD System: BCD stands for Binary Coded Decimal. In this system, each decimal digit (0 to 9) is represented separately by its 4-bit binary equivalent. Instead of representing the entire number as a single binary number, each decimal digit is encoded individually.

Difference from Pure Binary: In pure binary representation, the entire decimal number is converted into one binary number (e.g., decimal 9 is 1001, decimal 10 is 1010, decimal 1947 is 11110011011). BCD keeps each digit independent, so it’s easier to convert back to decimal.

Difference from Pure Binary: In pure binary representation, the entire decimal number is converted into one binary number (e.g., decimal 9 is 1001, decimal 10 is 1010, decimal 1947 is 11110011011). BCD keeps each digit independent, so it’s easier to convert back to decimal.
BCD Representation of 1947: Decimal digits: 1, 9, 4, 7 BCD: 1 → 0001 9 → 1001 4 → 0100 7 → 0111 So, 1947 in BCD = 0001 1001 0100 0111
BCD Representation of 1947: Decimal digits: 1, 9, 4, 7 BCD: 1 → 0001 9 → 1001 4 → 0100 7 → 0111 So, 1947 in BCD = 0001 1001 0100 0111
Advantages: Easier to convert to/from human-readable decimal numbers. Useful in digital displays like calculators and clocks. Reduces errors in decimal calculations caused by binary rounding.

sq.q: Represent the decimal number 57 in BCD format.
answer: 57 in decimal is represented as: 5 → 0101 7 → 0111 So, BCD = 0101 0111
